text:
pagerduty-bot: URGENT: High tail latency detected for tenant=\"frostline\" on dedicated-pool-3. 90th/95th token latency > 1.2s, error rate rising. Paging on-call.

jamie_oncall: on it. routing to eng-sre and eng-runtime. pulling logs now.

deploy-bot: Deploy window: no recent deploys in the last 30m to this pool.

ben_runtime: seeing a queue backlog for frostline across nodes gp3-0..gp3-3. batch sizes spiked, lots of max_batch_tokens=8192 requests queued.

rachel_sre: confirming customer impact: Clara, are you seeing errors from Frostline?

clara_cs: customer reports timeouts from several endpoints, some 500s. Customer on dedicated account, high SLA requirement. They're being paged internally.

jamie_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) isolate frostline to carve-out queue (soft-shed), 2) reduce max_batch_tokens for frostline to 2048, 3) increase scheduler weight to favor smaller batches, 4) enable burst capacity for pool if available. Will coordinate handoff.

ben_runtime: can run these from runtime console. Recommended order: set max_batch_tokens -> restart tenant scheduler -> apply temporary queue shaper.

jamie_oncall: doing step 1: applying tenant isolation rule to route new frostline requests to frostline-silo queue.

ben_runtime: applied. New request routing confirmed in trace logs.

jamie_oncall: step 2: lowering max_batch_tokens for frostline -> running CLI: 

```
redwoodctl tenant update --tenant frostline --set scheduler.max_batch_tokens=2048
```

ben_runtime: command accepted. patch rolled to runtime config. watch nn-*.logs for backpressure.

rachel_sre: step 3: applying scheduler shaper: reduce target_batch_window and increase preempt_threshold. CLI: 

```
redwoodctl scheduler tweak --pool dedicated-pool-3 --tenant frostline --target_batch_window=40 --preempt_threshold=0.6
```

ben_runtime: shaper applied, nodes report smaller average batch token counts. tail latency starting to fall (95th -> 720ms). error rate trending down.

clara_cs: customer confirmation: partial recovery, some endpoints still degraded but most traffic is succeeding. They want ETA on full recovery.

jamie_oncall: enabling burst capacity now to drain backlog (temporary).

deploy-bot: Burst capacity enabled on dedicated-pool-3: +2 instances for 10m.

ben_runtime: backlog drain visible — queue length down 78%. p95 down to ~410ms. no new 500 spikes in last 2m.

rachel_sre: good. mark incident as mitigated-in-progress. start preparing handoff notes for next on-call.

jamie_oncall: runtime note for handoff:
- Actions taken: tenant isolation -> frostline-silo; max_batch_tokens lowered 8192->2048; scheduler target_batch_window 120->40; preempt_threshold 0.3->0.6; burst capacity +2 for 10m.
- Observed effect: p95 1.2s -> 410ms over 6m, error rate down by 90%.
- Next steps: 1) keep shaper in place for 30m, 2) remove burst capacity after backlog drained, 3) coordinate with infra to provision longer-term capacity or advise customer on request shaping.

ben_runtime: logging config diffs to incident ticket #INC-9123. Reverting plan: if any signs of regression, revert max_batch_tokens to 4096 and re-evaluate.

clara_cs: relaying to Frostline: they're relieved, want a postmortem and permanent capacity plan. I'll set up an onboarding meeting.

jamie_oncall: tagging for follow-up: @eng-runtime to propose permanent knob settings & cost estimate, @product to advise on tenant-level autoscaling policy for dedicated pools.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: Jamie on-call until 5372471600. If you take over, update the incident status and handoff summary.

rachel_sre: taking over monitoring for now. If metrics hold for 30m, we'll resolve. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
